sources.note: Studentship page: eligibility, what is covered, exclusions, no separate application
Listing (award year 2026/27): about 10 awards, basis of award, awarding period, 217 courses
General eligibility rules, how to apply, timeline, notification
After the award: acceptance, other funding, visa, travel

summary: The Cambridge Trust Masters Studentship (International Fees) helps applicants with international fee status who take a one-year postgraduate course at the University of Cambridge in any subject. It covers the international-rate tuition fee only, plus the College fee for MASt courses. There is no separate application: you apply for admission by your course's funding deadline and ask to be considered for funding. The funding listing shows about 10 awards.
eligibility_notes:
Eligibility is by fee status, not nationality: applicants must have international (overseas) fee status. The course must be a one-year postgraduate course in any subject. Premium rate courses are excluded (the Trust names the MBA and MFin as courses it does not fund), and so are part-time MSt courses; MASt courses are eligible.

Not eligible: anyone who already holds, or is about to graduate with, a Master's or PhD-level qualification.

The studentship page does not describe a selection method. The funding listing says the basis of award is financial need (including hardship) and academic merit, and the Trust's general page says most scholarships need academic achievement and potential plus financial need. You need a conditional offer of admission. Cambridge's minimum for entry is a 2:1 UK Bachelor's degree or an international equivalent, and many courses ask for more. No funding is given for a degree at the same level as, or lower than, one you already hold (a required second MPhil before PhD is an exception), and students part-way through a Cambridge course cannot apply unless they apply for a higher degree after graduating.

Language: if English is not your first language, your course may need a test; see the requirements list.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work-experience requirement is stated. The Trust says applicants are not treated less favourably because of age.
funding_summary: The studentship pays the University tuition fee at the international rate, and the College fee for MASt courses only. The pages read list no maintenance, visa or health-surcharge payment. The funding listing gives no duration and says the award cannot be extended; the course itself is a one-year course.
programmes_note: One-year postgraduate study in any subject; premium rate courses and part-time MSt courses are excluded, MASt is eligible. The funding listing says 217 courses are covered, with a full list linked that did not open in the page text.
institutions_note: University of Cambridge only. The studentship can be held at any Cambridge College. On the application you may name up to two Colleges or leave it blank; the Trust does not choose the College or arrange accommodation.

summary.detail: One-year postgraduate courses in any subject (MASt included, part-time MSt excluded, premium rate courses excluded). The funding listing names Master's as the level and about 10 awards for award year 2026/27; a 2027/28 version of the listing was not found.
summary.source_text: one-year postgraduate study in any subject

benefits.limit_text: University tuition fee at the international rate
College fee, for MASt courses only
No maintenance or living allowance is listed
benefits.conditions: The studentship pages list tuition (and the MASt College fee) only. The Trust generally gives no allowance for spouses, children or dependants.

benefits.limit_text: Student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge are not mentioned for this studentship
benefits.conditions: The Trust's guidance says most scholars pay their own visa and health surcharge and the offer letter states whether the Trust covers them.

benefits.limit_text: Travel is paid only if the offer letter says so
benefits.conditions: Scholars otherwise arrange and pay for their own travel and accommodation.

requirements.text: Cambridge postgraduate admissions application submitted through the Applicant Portal by your course's funding deadline, with the funding section completed to say you wish to be considered for funding. A conditional offer of admission is needed. Each course needs its own application and documents. Agents' applications are not accepted. The application must be in English and Latin script.

Declare significant income from all sources (salaries, business profit, rents, dividends) in the funding section; the Trust says many awards need evidence of financial need, and the listing names financial need as a basis for this studentship.

Academic transcripts and certificates for every degree you have taken. If you are still studying, an interim or unofficial transcript is accepted and the final one is needed after an offer. Upload scanned originals; originals may be checked later through a verification service.

Two referees, entered in the Applicant Portal. They upload references in English through the Referee Portal by the application deadline; email and post are not accepted. Referees should be academic or professional depending on how long ago you left higher education (two academic referees if you are studying or left within 3 years). Do not name PhD students.
Curriculum vitae or resume, uploaded with the application.
Personal statement describing your skills, experience, academic achievements and motivation for the course.
Research proposal where the course asks for one, tailored to each course.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for courses that require a proposal

requirements.text: English test result (IELTS Academic, IELTS for UKVI Academic, IELTS One Skill Retake, IELTS Online, TOEFL iBT including Home Edition, or C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency for some courses). Scores come from the course page. Results must be dated no more than 2 years before the course starts. Test reports sent directly by IELTS or TOEFL are not accepted, and scores from different certificates cannot be combined. For LLM and MCL courses the evidence is needed when you apply.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if English is not your first language and not exempt (exemptions apply to nationals educated in a majority English-speaking country, or graduates of a 3-year UK-equivalent degree from such a country, excluding Canada). For most courses evidence is needed only after an offer.

requirements.text: Non-English documents must come with a full translation by a registered translator; do not translate them yourself. Upload PDFs under 2MB, not encrypted. Hard copies are not accepted.
Written work samples for courses that ask for them. GRE only if the course page says it is required; GMAT is not accepted by any course.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if the course page asks

requirements.text: Latest passport and any current or previous UK visas, uploaded to the Self-Service account after an offer so that the University can prepare the Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies.
requirements.conditional_rule: After an offer, for applicants who need a student visa

requirements.text: Application fee: GBP 85 per application for postgraduate degree courses other than doctoral courses, paid by Visa or MasterCard before submitting; a fee waiver may apply. The Trust cannot help with fees or waivers.

application_steps.title: Choose a one-year course and find its funding deadline
application_steps.detail: Pick an eligible one-year course in the Cambridge postgraduate directory and note its funding deadline, which is different from the application deadline. The main University funding deadlines for 2027/28 entry are 8 December 2026 and 6 January 2027; your course may differ. The complete application, including references, must be in by 23:59 GMT on the deadline.

application_steps.title: Check fee status and the Trust's rules
application_steps.detail: Make sure you expect international fee status (an assessment can be requested only after an offer) and that you do not hold, and are not about to gain, a Master's or PhD-level qualification. You may name up to two Colleges or leave it blank. Apply for every scholarship that suits you, because funding is highly competitive.

application_steps.title: Submit the admissions application and ask for funding
application_steps.detail: In the Applicant Portal fill every section, upload your documents, pay the fee and tick that you wish to apply for funding. Declare significant income. No separate studentship form is needed. The Trust cannot add information after you submit, though extra documents can be uploaded to your self-service account.

application_steps.title: Department assesses your admission application
application_steps.detail: The department or faculty reviews your application, may interview you and recommends admission. The Degree Committee approves (about 10 days) and the Postgraduate Admissions Office issues a conditional offer (about 10 days, longer at peak times). Admission offers start from November at the earliest.

application_steps.title: Trust awards studentships on need and merit
application_steps.detail: The funding listing gives the basis of award as financial need (including hardship) and academic merit. The Trust does not take part in admission or College choice. The awarding period runs from the beginning of March (listing) or mid-February (Trust page) to the end of July; most awards are made in February and March.

application_steps.title: Wait for the offer; no news by end of July means unsuccessful
application_steps.detail: The Trust gives no updates on individual applications and will say on its website when main offers are finished. Awards not taken up are reallocated, so you stay under consideration until the end of July. If you have not heard by then, assume you were unsuccessful. Unsuccessful applicants are not notified and get no individual feedback.

application_steps.title: Return the response form and meet admission conditions
application_steps.detail: Read the offer letter and keep a copy; it may serve as proof of funding for a student visa. Return the response form before its deadline, because the scholarship is not final until the Trust has it. Meet all admission conditions on time (for an October start, the conditions deadline is 31 July) and accept the admission offer in the Self-Service account.

application_steps.title: Arrange visa, travel and arrival
application_steps.detail: Obtain a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies from the University (expected in June for an October start; none is issued for part-time programmes such as the MSt) and apply for the student visa, with ATAS clearance if your course needs it. Plan your own accommodation and travel unless your offer letter says otherwise.

application_steps.title: Tell the Trust about other funding
application_steps.detail: Scholarships must be taken up in the year awarded and usually cannot be deferred. Tell the Trust about any other funding offered before or during the award; a full-cost award from another source can end the Trust offer, and a partial award can lead to an adjusted value.
